title: Author wins $6,200 from Anthropic for stealing his books — but years of fighting have made him 'much poorer'
excerpt: AI company settles the class-action case as its IPO draws near.
content_html:
Charles Graeber knows that what he and a group of other authors accomplished was epic.

Together, they took on AI giant Anthropic in a class-action lawsuit that resulted in one of the largest copyright infringement settlements of all time. But he's still not ready to claim victory.

Must Read

  • Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

  • Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake — here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

  • The tax breaks in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' expire after 2028 — and experts say most people won't act in time. What to do before the window closes

The author of the bestselling true crime book The Good Nurse — along with fellow writers Andrea Bartz and Kirk Wallace Johnson — were among those whose lawsuit led Claude maker Anthropic to agree to a $1.5 billion settlement in July, roughly two years after the authors sued the company.

But the agreement was only a partial victory. On a personal level, Graeber said it came at a steep cost.

Lawyers will get a portion of the settlement while thousands of authors will split what's left.

Graeber said he'll receive $3,100 for each of the two books Anthropic used without authorization to train the large language model behind the Claude chatbot. In the end, though, that's not as much as it sounds.

"A lot of travel, a lot of discussion about what to do and how to proceed and a lot of jobs passed up," Graeber told NPR. "I'm much poorer for this settlement, ironically."

A win or a loss?

While the AI company agreed to pay a near-record amount, the case was hardly a win for authors.

The court ruled that Anthropic did not violate copyright law simply by training its AI models on copyrighted books. Instead, the company was held liable for using unauthorized copies of those works.

AI companies, including Anthropic, have argued that the fair use doctrine allows them to use copyrighted material without permission in certain circumstances. Authors have countered that fair use doesn't apply because AI systems are trained on their work to generate new writing that could compete with the originals.

A machine that can produce a book in minutes or hours has an inherent advantage over human authors, they argue. Graeber, for example, spent a decade researching and writing The Good Nurse, which Netflix has since adapted into a film.

"I felt very small," he told People in 2025. "I'm one person and this is a huge tech company that didn't feel the need to even notify me that they wanted or were using several books."

content_html_zh:
查尔斯·格雷伯知道他和其他一群作家所取得的成就是史诗般的。

他们共同对人工智能巨头 Anthropic 提起集体诉讼，最终达成了有史以来最大的版权侵权和解协议之一。 但他还没有准备好宣布胜利。

必读

  • 杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 支持一个平台，让任何人都可以以低至 100 美元的价格投资出租房屋——无需真正成为房东即可像房东一样积累财富的 6 种方法
  • Dave Ramsey 警告说，近 50% 的美国人在社会保障方面犯了 1 个重大错误——这就是它的本质，以及尽快修复它的 3 个简单步骤
  • 特朗普“美丽大法案”中的税收减免将于 2028 年到期，专家表示大多数人不会及时采取行动。 窗口关闭之前可以做什么

畅销真实犯罪小说《好护士》的作者以及其他作家安德里亚·巴茨 (Andrea Bartz) 和柯克·华莱士·约翰逊 (Kirk Wallace Johnson) 都在诉讼中，导致克劳德 (Claude) 的制作人 Anthropic 在 7 月同意支付 15 亿美元的和解金，大约在作者起诉该公司两年后。

但该协议只是部分胜利。 格雷伯表示，就个人而言，这付出了高昂的代价。

律师将获得部分和解金，而数以千计的作者将瓜分剩下的钱。

Graeber 表示，Anthropic 未经授权使用两本书来训练 Claude 聊天机器人背后的大型语言模型，他将获得每本 3,100 美元的报酬。 但最终，这并不像听起来那么严重。

格雷伯告诉美国国家公共广播电台：“我们进行了大量的旅行，进行了大量关于该做什么以及如何进行的讨论，并且放弃了很多工作。” “讽刺的是，这个和解让我变得更穷了。”

是赢还是输？

尽管这家人工智能公司同意支付接近创纪录的金额，但对于作者来说，这个案子并不是一个胜利。

法院裁定，Anthropic 仅在受版权保护的书籍上训练其人工智能模型并不违反版权法。 相反，该公司因使用这些作品的未经授权的副本而承担责任。

包括 Anthropic 在内的人工智能公司辩称，合理使用原则允许他们在某些情况下未经许可使用受版权保护的材料。 作者反驳说，合理使用并不适用，因为人工智能系统经过训练，可以生成可以与原作竞争的新作品。

他们认为，能够在几分钟或几小时内写出一本书的机器比人类作者具有固有的优势。 例如，格雷伯花了十年时间研究和撰写《好护士》，Netflix 此后将其改编成电影。

“我感觉自己很渺小，”他在 2025 年告诉《人物》杂志。 “我是一个人，这是一家大型科技公司，他们甚至不需要通知我他们想要或正在使用几本书。”
